text.p: Peter Shilton, who will create English soccer history by making his 1,000th League appearance when he turns out for Leyton Orient against Brighton on Sunday, aims to extend his playing career well past his latest landmark.
The 47-year-old former England keeper, who has 125 caps, said on Friday he was addicted to football and, as long as he feels the urge to play, he will keep doing so.
"When you get to my age, you don't look too far ahead," he said.
"But the way the games are going at Leyton Orient, I don't feel too bad after matches, so who knows?
"I'm contracted until the end of the season, so I'll play until then and see how it goes."
The one-time Leicester, Nottingham Forest, Southampton and Derby star is particularly proud of being about to become the first British player to clock up 1,000 League appearances.
"I've spent more than 30 years in professional football and it is obviously a fine achievement. I'm looking forward to it," he said.
"I think when you love something so much, and love competing and winning football games, it is something that is very difficult to give up.
"But as long as I feel I'm doing myself justice and not letting anybody down, then I will continue to play. It is the third division, but you've still got to make the saves.
"I'm getting a great deal of satisfaction through playing and competing and staying involved in the game.
"I would like to get back into management -- but only when I finish playing. That's the best thing you can do in football. It is impossible to say how long I can go on, but I feel as fit as ever."
Shilton is hoping that Orient chairman Barry Hearn has not planned any surprises for him on Sunday.
"I read in one of the newspapers that I might be coming in a parachute, but I don't like heights," he said.
His greatest memories are winning the European Cup with Forest in 1979 and 1980 and reaching the World Cup semi-finals with England in 1990.
"At club level it was winning the European Cup two years running," he said. "That was a fantastic achievement for such an unfashionable club. We had just come out of the old first division.
"For England, it was reaching the semi-finals of the World Cup in Italy. That was a great achievement and a terrific match to play in."

Shilton started playing before most of today's professionals were even born. He made his first division debut for Leicester at the age of 16 in May 1966 -- two months before England won the World Cup and a year before the Beatles released Sergeant Pepper.

At one time he was England's highest earning player, but lost a fortune in gambling and the property market. As well as playing, he was manager of Plymouth for three years from 1992 before leaving under a cloud. He has not managed a club since.

His 999 league games to date have been with Leicester 286 games, Stoke 110; Nottingham Forest 202, Southampton 188, Derby 175, Plymouth 34, Bolton one and Orient 3. In all he has played a total of 1,371 first class matches -- a record that is unlikely ever to be equalled, and one that Shilton has every intention of adding to for as long as he possibly can.
